SMTO-SKL-0002 — A Skill setting has a value SMTO can't accept

GUID: 1f4b0dd3-6d11-4939-92bb-30016e4ad37c
Slug: skill-configuration-schema-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: skl

What happened

  • One of the settings for this Skill isn't in a form the Skill accepts, such as a number that's too big or a required box left empty. Your change wasn't saved, so the earlier settings are still in use.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the message in the Skill's settings window. After "Invalid configuration at" it names the setting that's wrong and the rule it broke, such as maximum. SMTO stops at the first setting that breaks a rule, so that's the one to fix.
  2. Change that setting to an allowed value. The notes under each setting help; for example, Timeout must be 1 to 30 seconds and Results 1 to 10. Each setting has fixed limits, and a value outside them can't be saved.
  3. Select Save. If your edits get confusing, select Reload saved configuration to start again from the settings currently in use. Reload throws away unsaved edits and shows exactly what SMTO is using now.

What success looks like

  • The settings window says "Saved. Future calls use this configuration."

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep selecting Save with the same values; they will be refused the same way. Never type a password or API key directly into a setting.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Skill configuration validation failed because the submitted (or stored, or canonicalized) configuration does not match the Skill's declared JSON schema; the message names the first failing path and the rule it broke.

What this means

  • Public Skill configuration or its canonicalized result fails the advertised JSON schema. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Public Skill configuration or its canonicalized result fails the advertised JSON schema.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the safe field path and schema validator reported without copying secret input.

How to fix it

  • Read the path and rule named after "Invalid configuration at" (for example /defaults/result_count with maximum) and correct that field against the Skill's json_schema in its SkillConfigurationDefinition (for Web, WebConfiguration in src/agent_runtime/skills/web/models.py). If the stored entry itself is invalid, the editor loads defaults with a repair warning without overwriting it; save a valid replacement through the editor.
  • Correct the indicated field in the Skill configuration editor using the advertised schema. Keep secret values in Parameter Store references.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended configuration validates before it is saved.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
